extraction_policy: Generalized from local workspace structure, docs, code identifiers, JSON schema keys, and GitHub repository metadata. Do not store copied source code or project prose here.

cards.name: Pressure arena with event clouds
cards.summary: A run enters a thematic arena that samples event threads, reactions, cascades, and exits based on state rather than following a fixed mission list.
questions: What pressure defines the arena?
Which actions should echo later?
What makes the arena release or collapse?
risks: Too abstract unless each event has a concrete situation
State can become invisible to the player

cards.name: Delayed consequence stack
cards.summary: Choices create hooks that mature after intervening scenes, turning old decisions into later complications, allies, costs, or altered routes.
questions: What must happen before the payoff can trigger?
Is the payoff readable without spoiling it?
Can the hook grow or be pruned?

cards.name: Narrow source packet pipeline
cards.summary: A local tool builds a bounded packet from schemas, source motifs, constraints, and acceptance gates before any writing agent drafts content.
questions: What exact context is enough?
Which IDs must remain stable?
How will the returned patch be validated?

cards.name: Corpus pattern extraction
cards.summary: Source material is converted into setup, pressure, reversal, cost, sensory anchor, and residue instead of being copied into game text.
questions: What action pattern survives after names and prose are removed?
What does the source teach the player to do?
risks: Decorative source references without mechanical effect

cards.name: Validation-first content integration
cards.summary: Generated or migrated content is accepted only after schema checks, action handler checks, payoff audits, and runtime smoke tests.
questions: Which action IDs are real?
What can break silently?
Which test proves the player can see it?
risks: Validators that do not model player flow

cards.name: Text console plus command parser
cards.summary: A dense mobile-friendly console presents room text, resource state, command input, and choice buttons while runtime managers own consequences.
questions: What must fit on one portrait screen?
Which commands bypass buttons?
How are resource changes narrated?

cards.name: Deck-driven run pressure
cards.summary: Decks, cooldowns, thresholds, and resource counters choose what pressure appears next and when the run tips toward warning, lock, or ending.
questions: Which axis escalates fastest?
What does the player spend to delay pressure?
How does deck composition change after choices?

cards.name: Multi-use power mutation
cards.summary: A power is designed with at least one encounter use, one out-of-encounter use, and one delayed surprising use so it changes both tactics and story routes.
questions: What does this power solve immediately?
What does it contaminate or reveal later?
How can an old power surprise the player?

cards.name: Touch lane combat with buffered intent
cards.summary: Mobile swipes resolve into planar lanes, target selection, buffered attacks, dash commitments, blocks, and hit reactions.
questions: What makes a swipe miss fairly?
Which moves can buffer?
How does the camera show commitment?

cards.name: Contact-to-duel handoff
cards.summary: Overworld contact shifts into a closer committed combat presentation instead of resolving as generic collision damage.
questions: When does the handoff interrupt movement?
What information must survive the camera shift?
How does escape work?

cards.name: Survivorlike offer loop
cards.summary: Repeated pressure waves grant move, power, route, or resource offers that reshape the build while enemies keep the player moving.
questions: What does the player choose under pressure?
Which offers change input rhythm?
How does a build become visually legible?

cards.name: Conditional artifact recipes
cards.summary: Artifacts unlock when the run gathers state tokens, components, or behavior evidence, then create new constraints or exits.
questions: What did the player prove to earn this?
What does the artifact demand after it helps?
Can it alter a later arena?

cards.name: Operational report encounter packet
cards.summary: Each encounter arrives as detection, reports, authorization choice, operation result, and later crew/system consequence.
questions: Who reports the situation?
What does command authorize?
What system records the aftermath?

cards.name: Local review surface
cards.summary: A lightweight local web view renders cards, rooms, docs, or data records for fast human review without launching the full game.
questions: What can the reviewer judge fastest?
Which fields should be filterable?
Can data edits refresh quickly?
risks: Review UI diverges from game runtime

cards.name: Nondestructive writing lab
cards.summary: Original text is preserved while critique, drift analysis, lost-material detection, and revisions are stored as separate reports or drafts.
questions: What should never be overwritten?
What counts as evidence?
How does critique become an edit plan?

cards.name: Audio manifest and playback sync
cards.summary: Spoken lines are normalized, deduped, generated into manifests, and smoke-tested against text playback so audio remains aligned with content.
questions: Which text is spoken versus displayed?
What invalidates a clip?
How does playback recover from scrub/skip?

cards.name: Vehicle or body as dungeon
cards.summary: A constrained moving vessel, body, machine, or route becomes the dungeon, making navigation, repair, threat, and identity overlap.
questions: What spaces are organs or systems?
What does movement cost?
Can repair become transformation?

cards.name: Mechanical creature board ecosystem
cards.summary: Creature-like pieces, hazards, and board state interact through readable rules, creating a tabletop-feeling tactics loop.
questions: What can each piece do at a glance?
Which rule creates surprise?
What state is visible without UI clutter?

cards.name: Portable web choice player
cards.summary: A static or local-server web player loads JSON content, handles saves, renders choices, and supports quick packaging or review.
questions: What content can ship as JSON?
How are saves migrated?
What can be tested without a backend?

cards.name: Highway vehicle survivorlike
cards.summary: The player survives on a forward-moving road while generated terrain, fuel/harvest stops, raiders, chasers, and road hazards pressure speed and lane commitment.
questions: What forces the player to change lanes?
What resource makes stopping tempting?
How do enemies rearm after contact?
risks: Driving model too complex for the camera

cards.name: Layered vehicle audio model
cards.summary: Engine, tire roll, slip, skid, throttle, surface, and wind layers are sourced, looped, normalized, attributed, and mixed from runtime vehicle parameters.
questions: Which parameter controls each layer?
What audio must loop seamlessly?
How is attribution tracked?

cards.name: Cockpit HUD gesture zones
cards.summary: A first-person or dashboard view turns screen regions into accelerate, turbo, stop, reverse, weapon, and settings affordances while preserving vehicle readability.
questions: Which zones can be operated without looking away?
How does the player know current gear or intent?
What belongs in HUD versus world?

cards.name: Pursuer rearm gap
cards.summary: Enemies that collide, ram, shoot, or harvest the player expose stop buffers, rearm distances, contact damage caps, and retreat/approach states so repeated hits feel fair.
questions: How far must an enemy reset before it can hit again?
Can the player read when contact is armed?
What converts contact into harvest, flee, or death?

cards.name: Asset sourcing manifest pipeline
cards.summary: Generated, downloaded, extracted, and imported assets are tracked by source, license, processing step, and target use so prototypes can move fast without losing provenance.
questions: What can be regenerated?
What needs attribution?
Which assets are placeholders versus canonical?

cards.name: Pose lab animation retargeting
cards.summary: Imported 2D/3D skeletons, clip profiles, bone maps, onion poses, and transform controls become a lightweight lab for inspecting and adapting motion.
questions: Which bones are editable controls?
What interpolation is safe for the imported clip?
How can motion be compared across clips?
risks: Tool controls drifting from runtime rig

cards.name: Mining/shop/upgrade microloop
cards.summary: A compact Godot loop combines map generation, mining or harvesting, shop offers, upgrades, enemy pressure, and extraction into a small repeatable run.
questions: What resource changes movement or combat?
When does the shop appear?
What pushes the player to leave?
risks: Map generation with no tactical texture

cards.name: Phone-first canvas release workbench
cards.summary: A browser game is built, tested, packaged, and uploaded from Android/Termux so mobile feel is the primary validation surface rather than a late port.
questions: What must be verified on the actual phone before desktop polish?
Which artifacts need Android media refresh before external upload?
Can the release package be rebuilt from source without hidden local files?
risks: Shared storage has executable-bit and git-hook limitations
Android upload pickers may not see new files until media indexing refreshes
Canvas UI may fail inside itch fullscreen/iframe unless DOM overlays are tested

cards.name: Recursive knockback dash core
cards.summary: A movement burst from rest does not directly kill enemies; it launches them as physics-like projectiles that kill on wall or enemy impact and can propagate chains.
questions: When does the dash rearm?
How much target bias prevents near misses without feeling fake?
What visual/audio feedback separates launch, chain impact, wall kill, and player death?
risks: If ram kills directly, chain play disappears
If knockback is too weak, the player dies after a successful hit
If target bias is hidden, misses feel arbitrary

cards.name: Bounded AI release scribe
cards.summary: Claude or another writing model drafts release/page/devlog copy only from a narrow packet, while Codex or the integrator validates facts and applies the final artifact.
questions: Which facts are safe to advertise?
What claims must not be invented?
Where will raw and integrated outputs live for traceability?
risks: Draft can overstate release status or asset generation details
Pretty prose can smuggle unsupported claims
Publishing without route verification leaves stale/generated content invisible

cards.name: Generated asset provenance loop
cards.summary: Generated raster art, music, and synthesized SFX become project assets only after placement, manifest/provenance capture, local validation, and external-file visibility refresh where needed.
questions: Is this preview-only or project-bound?
Which manifest owns this asset?
Does the consuming runtime path point inside the project rather than a tool cache?
risks: Assets left under tool cache vanish from project handoff
External upload pickers can miss newly copied files
Transparent-background assets need validation for alpha/fringing

cards.name: Tap/hold missile-command survivorlike
cards.summary: A phone-first fixed-base defense game maps tap and hold to distinct but overlapping weapon rhythms: taps fire ready interceptors, holds maintain automatic fire, and wave-clears offer build upgrades.
questions: What fires on tap versus hold?
How does the player read which racks are ready?
Which upgrades change input rhythm rather than only damage numbers?
risks: Cooldowns can feel unresponsive without semi-auto forgiveness
HUD buttons can crowd a phone playfield
Enemy HP needs visible armor rings or it reads as missed input

cards.name: Branching airborne enemy family
cards.summary: One enemy type breaks into another threat instead of simply dying: a heavy carrier can spawn a slower active attacker, whose projectiles are smaller and separately destructible.
questions: Does breaking the carrier help now but add a new short-term threat?
Are child projectiles visually and mechanically distinct from main missiles?
Can all player damage systems hit every hostile class?
risks: If carrier and child both die instantly, the branch is invisible
If child projectiles are too similar to missiles, targeting priority becomes muddy
Separate enemy arrays can be missed by collision or wave-clear checks

cards.name: Visible kill-chain multiplier
cards.summary: Rapid kills within a short timer increase score through a visible chain counter, then expire or reset on base damage to turn clean defense into a score-chasing layer.
questions: What resets the chain besides time?
Can the player see the multiplier while aiming?
Does the audio climb long enough for the player to perceive it?
risks: Score hooks can miss some kill paths unless centralized
Combo HUD can distract if it competes with survival data

cards.name: WebAudio buffer SFX bus with runtime mute
cards.summary: Game SFX are decoded into WebAudio buffers, varied by pitch/gain, routed through a compressor and output gain, and controlled by a persistent SFX toggle separate from music.
questions: Does volume reduction happen after compression as well as before?
Are one-shots suppressed when SFX is muted?
Can music and SFX be toggled independently after browser audio unlock?
risks: A compressor can mask source-gain changes
Browser/itch caches can hide script changes without cache busting
Creating Audio objects at trigger time causes latency

cards.name: Generated canvas background and sprite-sheet loop
cards.summary: AI-generated bitmap backgrounds and chroma-key sprite sheets become durable canvas assets through copy-to-project, alpha/key validation, atlas metadata, manifest provenance, and runtime fallback drawing.
questions: Is the asset preview-only or runtime-bound?
Which crop/focus keeps phone and desktop readable?
What happens if the generated image fails to load?
risks: Generated sheet regions can overlap or mis-center
Background art can reduce gameplay contrast
Leaving assets in generator cache breaks release packaging

cards.name: Cache-busted itch HTML release
cards.summary: A static HTML/canvas game release is packaged as a zip, integrity-checked, uploaded through locally built Termux butler, and script-cache-busted so hosted iframe/mobile playback reflects changes.
questions: Does the zip include every runtime asset type?
Is the hosted script URL cache-busted for this version?
Did butler status show the expected build/version?
risks: Itch/mobile browser cache can hide updated JS
Official Linux ARM64 butler may not run under Android linker
New files in shared storage may not appear in upload pickers until refreshed

cards.name: Additive trait mutation stack
cards.summary: Run upgrades add orthogonal flags, levels, caps, and scalar modifiers that compose at action resolution time instead of replacing each other.
ingredients: snapshot active traits onto spawned objects
explicit replacement language only when behavior is exclusive
questions: Does this upgrade remove any behavior the player already earned?
Can the spawned object snapshot traits so future upgrades do not retroactively affect it?
Where does the composed action resolve: launch, hit, tick, or death?
Which nested values need UI deltas when the player takes this again?
risks: Stacking can become unreadable without concrete UI deltas
Composed effects can double-dip damage unless each trait owns a clear scalar
Exclusive enum fields accidentally turn additive upgrades into replacements
Old projectiles may mutate mid-flight if traits are not snapshotted
